html:
The Epic of Manas is the great oral epic of the Kyrgyz people, and the longest known epic poem. Its hero Manas unites the scattered Kyrgyz tribes and leads them against their enemies, among them the Kalmaks, the Oirat Mongols.

It was sung, not written. Performers called manaschi learned it by ear and could recite it for days. Its oldest layers may go back centuries; the chart's date of 1792 marks an early written mention of the hero in a Persian manuscript. The epic has three parts, following Manas, his son Semetei and his grandson Seitek.

Scholars first wrote down parts of it in the 1800s: the Kazakh traveller Chokan Valikhanov and the German scholar Wilhelm Radloff. Full versions from great manaschi were recorded in the 1900s. Manas is now a national symbol of Kyrgyzstan, and UNESCO lists it as world heritage.
